scope: A coherent exploratory pass. Existing repositories read only. No empirical discovery, new microscopic theory, MOND derivation or AeST evolution claimed.

claim_classes.established_result: Mathematical identity or published result within its explicit assumptions.
claim_classes.conditional_model: A physical-model prediction or reduction conditional on its equations, initial state and regime.
claim_classes.untested_conjecture: An application or mechanism not established by a derivation or observation in this pass.
claim_classes.own_inference: This pass's mathematical example, comparison, interpretation or proposed discriminating probe. No priority claimed.

sources.title: Optimal prediction with memory
sources.authors: Alexandre J. Chorin, Ole H. Hald and Raz Kupferman
sources.locator: Section 2, equations 1-7, printed pages 240-242; section 6, orthogonal dynamics; section 7, short-memory approximations.
sources.inspection: Read full-text extracted derivation of the Liouville formulation, conditional and linear projections, Dyson formula, exact generalized Langevin equation and short-memory assumptions. PDF page 3 was also requested through screenshot, but the evidence used here is the extracted text.
sources.supports: The nonlinear Mori-Zwanzig identity separates instantaneous evolution, history and an orthogonal term determined by full initial data. Projection and initial ensemble specify the description. Practical approximation is a separate step.
sources.limits: Formal projection does not independently solve the orthogonal dynamics or establish physical thermal noise. Infinite-dimensional applications need analytical assumptions. Our finite block derivation and closure criterion are elementary independent calculations, not a new theorem credited to this paper.

sources.title: Nonlinear generalized Langevin equations
sources.locator: Publisher abstract; Journal of Statistical Physics 9, pages 215-220.
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract and bibliographic information only. Full text was subscription restricted and was not acquired.
sources.supports: Exact generalized Langevin equations are derived for nonlinear systems interacting with specified heat baths. The abstract separately identifies an approximately Markovian example.
sources.limits: Used only for its stated model scope and historical credit. No bath Hamiltonian, fluctuation-dissipation formula or detailed derivation is attributed to uninspected full text.

sources.title: Non-Markovian quantum dynamics and the method of correlated projection superoperators
sources.locator: Section II.1, equations 3-14; section II.2, equation 15 and propagator caveat; section III.3, equation 31.
sources.inspection: Read standard projection, Nakajima-Zwanzig kernel, the assumptions used for the displayed homogeneous equation, time-convolutionless representation and correlated-initial-state discussion.
sources.supports: The partial trace can be represented by an idempotent superoperator on the joint state. Initial-state compatibility controls an inhomogeneous term. A time-local representation can describe non-Markovian dynamics and can fail at singular times.
sources.limits: The paper's simplified interaction-picture homogeneous equation uses additional assumptions. We use independent constant-generator block algebra in the report instead of generalizing those simplifications. Time dependence of a generator alone is not a sufficient witness of non-Markovianity. arXiv's HTML generated date is not the paper's publication date.

sources.title: Operational Markov condition for quantum processes
sources.authors: Felix A. Pollock, Cesar Rodriguez-Rosario, Thomas Frauenheim, Mauro Paternostro and Kavan Modi
sources.locator: Main operational definition and theorem, equation 2; Appendix B.3, two-swap construction; Appendix B.1-B.2 for narrower diagnostics.
sources.inspection: Read the causal-break definition, main theorem, divisibility discussion and the explicit two-swap counterexample in Appendix B.3.
sources.supports: Past controls can alter the future after the system is re-prepared in the same state. Two swaps provide memory without system-environment correlations at the sampled discrete stages.
sources.limits: A statement about an operational quantum process with allowed controls and specified sampling. It is not equivalent to every two-time non-Markovianity measure. Product states at discrete stages do not exclude correlations during a physical continuous implementation of a swap. This pass reproduces the authors' example with a system reset; it is not a novel construction.

sources.title: A Unified Framework for Multiscale Modeling using the Mori-Zwanzig Formalism and the Variational Multiscale Method
sources.authors: Eric J. Parish and Karthik Duraisamy
sources.locator: Section 3.1, equations 21-35; section 4 on orthogonal dynamics; section 6.2 on dissipativity; section 6.3, equations 98-103.
sources.inspection: Read the linear integrating-factor elimination, remarks about cost, orthogonal-dynamics limitations, dissipation caveat and finite-memory upwind-flux construction.
sources.supports: Fine-scale elimination produces an exact coarse equation with memory. Approximation choices can reproduce known stabilization terms. A selected finite-memory model gives the upwind correction for linear advection.
sources.limits: The upwind equivalence uses a specific discontinuous Galerkin setting and memory-length choice. It is not a general equivalence between all physical viscosity and information loss. No generic sign of dissipation is established.

sources.title: Introduction to Effective Field Theory
sources.locator: Section 2.1, scalar model and locality discussion, especially equation 20; section 2.2, Wilson action.
sources.inspection: Read the tree-level heavy-field elimination and local inverse-mass expansion, its decoupling assumptions and the Wilson-action definitions.
sources.supports: An exact eliminated-field expression can be nonlocal while its controlled low-energy expansion yields local interactions. Regime and scale hierarchy matter.
sources.limits: A low-energy scattering effective action is not automatically a retarded initial-value equation. The report's causal-boundary warning is a distinction in interpretation, not a claim that this source derives an AeST memory kernel or MOND law.

sources.title: New Relativistic Theory for Modified Newtonian Dynamics
sources.locator: Phenomenological requirements and equation 2; cosmological observables, equations 7-12 and paragraph immediately after equation 11.
sources.inspection: Independently read the fluid-variable definitions, perturbation evolution, pressure contrast, explicit nonclosure paragraph and prescribed low-gradient action limit.
sources.supports: Effective density and velocity equations have fluid form while the pressure depends on vector perturbations alpha and E. The low-gradient functional behavior is selected to obtain MOND phenomenology.
sources.limits: This is a linear cosmological perturbation result within AeST. It does not establish nonlinear shock thermodynamics, a halo memory time, an effective thermal equation of state, or radiative trapping. Gauge and constraint reduction must precede a proposed matched-state test.

sources.title: Quantum Darwinism in an Everyday Environment: Huge Redundancy in Scattered Photons
sources.authors: C. Jess Riedel and Wojciech H. Zurek
sources.locator: Figure 2(b), equations 17-18, paragraphs on perfectly isotropic illumination.
sources.inspection: Independently read the figure caption and isotropic-limit calculation after the relations route supplied this lead.
sources.supports: Decoherence and accessible redundant records are distinct in a specified photon-scattering model.
sources.limits: Perfectly mixed directional illumination is a special limit. This source alone does not analyze a general operational feedback-memory criterion. The fresh-fragment comparison in our report is an elementary channel argument with explicit additional assumptions.

sources.title: ASASSN-24fw: Candidate gas-rich circumsecondary disk occultation of a main-sequence star
sources.locator: Section III.1, period-alias discussion after figures 5-6.
sources.inspection: Independently read the DASCH period discussion and ASAS phase-coverage exclusion of P/2 after the evidence route supplied this lead.
sources.supports: Additional phase coverage excludes a period alias left unresolved by the archival data alone.
sources.limits: This is an inference about candidate periods, not evidence that a physical history-dependent force caused the eclipse. It does not uniquely identify the occulting structure.

sources.title: Foundation-0/gravity claim C-26 and research notebook fluid analogy
sources.locator: CLAIMS.md lines 128-140, especially line 136; notebook lines 38-54.
sources.inspection: Read matching claim and notebook passages locally; not an independent observational source.
sources.supports: The project proposes a post-caustic entropy-conserving fluid treatment and explicitly labels its AeST application a conjecture.
sources.limits: Numerical scale matches do not establish closure, dissipation, entropy production or stability. These files were not edited.

sources.title: Expedition route reports: relations, persistence and evidence
sources.inspection: Read report text and targeted source-relevant passages. Checked AeST, photon-record and period-alias primary passages independently.
sources.supports: Route continuity and leads connecting fluid closure, environment records and complementary observation channels.
sources.limits: Peer reports are not independent primary evidence. Hidden-dynamics findings do not broaden their physical claims.

sources.title: Exact block elimination, two-variable closure, stationary Gaussian memory and two-swap probes
sources.inspection: Ran standard-library Python calculation and built-in assertions; analytic solution compared with full RK4 and independent scalar Volterra quadrature at four steps; exact covariance and small-matrix algebra checked.
sources.supports: Equivalent retained dynamics under elimination; insufficiency of a scalar deterministic state; accuracy limits of instantaneous closure; a stationary Gaussian conditional-memory witness; identical static but different transient responses; Pollock two-swap reproduction with reset.
sources.limits: No measured data, no stochastic trajectory simulation, no AeST equations, no microscopic identification from a fitted kernel. The Gaussian result assumes the specified stationary linear process, independent white driving, exact samples and no measurement noise. The swap result assumes ideal discrete swaps, a pure independent environment initially and a system-only reset.

strongest_result.claim: Exact elimination of coupled dynamical degrees of freedom is a shared mathematical operation that can generate history dependence across otherwise different theories.
strongest_result.boundary: This establishes a common operation, not a common microscopic mechanism. Memory depends on the retained state, preparation, measurements and interventions.

proposed_next_probes.name: Constraint-reduced linear AeST closure test
proposed_next_probes.description: Fix gauge and constraints, identify allowed full states sharing the candidate fluid variables, vary independent vector modes, and compare pressure and retained evolution.
proposed_next_probes.would_strengthen: A measured long-lived difference would establish insufficiency of that particular fluid closure in the tested linear regime.
proposed_next_probes.would_weaken: Absence of independent allowed hidden states, or fast relaxation with a uniform error bound, could justify a restricted closure.

proposed_next_probes.name: Witness Map companion separating interference, records and feedback
proposed_next_probes.description: Compare outgoing fresh fragments with recycled fragments and a controlled reset. Measure coherence, fragment information and conditional future dependence separately.
proposed_next_probes.would_strengthen: One model exhibiting independent changes in the three quantities would make the distinctions directly inspectable.
proposed_next_probes.would_weaken: A restricted physical environment might relate them quantitatively, but this would not make the relation universal.
